'''Hermann Schmalzried''' (born 21 January 1932 in [[Koblenz]]) is a German chemist known for his work in physical chemistry, especially on the thermodynamics and kinetics of solid state chemistry.

== Education and career ==

Schmalzried received his diploma (with a diploma thesis on the fluorescence of [[benzopyrene]]) from [[Theodor Förster]] at the [[University of Stuttgart]] and received his doctorate in 1958 at the Roentgen Institute of the University of Stuttgart with [[Richard Glocker]] (1890-1978) and was a postdoc with [[Carl Wagner]] at the Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry in Göttingen, a pioneer in [[Solid-state chemistry|solid state chemistry]]. He habilitated in 1966 at the [[Leibniz University Hannover]] on the topic of disorder in ternary ionic crystals. In 1966, he became a full professor at the [[Technical University of Clausthal]] and in 1975 at the Leibniz University Hannover. He was Courtesy Professor at [[Cornell University]] and Schottky Professor at [[Stanford University]].<ref name=Stuttgart>{{Cite web |title=Reden anlässlich der Verleihung der Ehrenpromotion (Dr. rer. nat. E. h.) an Prof. Dr. rer. nat. Hermann Schmalzried durch die Universität Stuttgart |url=https://elib.uni-stuttgart.de/bitstream/11682/6032/1/Inhalt_Schmalzried.pdf}}</ref><ref name=AE>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Schmalzried Hermann |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Schmalzried_Hermann |access-date=2022-08-20 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>

He wrote two textbooks on [[chemical reaction]]s in solids, which were internationally standard works. He also dealt with thermodynamics of solids and [[electrochemistry]]. His group worked closely with [[Alan Lidiard]]'s group in [[England]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lidiard |first=Alan B. |date=2003 |title=70 years of defect physical chemistry |url=https://xlink.rsc.org/?DOI=B301881B |journal=Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. |language=en |volume=5 |issue=11 |pages=2161–2163 |doi=10.1039/B301881B |issn=1463-9076|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Grout |first1=Peter |last2=Catlow |first2=Richard |last3=Grimes |first3=Robin |date=2021-05-04 |title=Alan Lidiard |journal=Philosophical Magazine Letters |language=en |volume=101 |issue=5 |pages=183–184 |doi=10.1080/09500839.2021.1908638 |bibcode=2021PMagL.101..183G |s2cid=234347042 |issn=0950-0839|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==

Schmalzried received the Wilhelm Jost Memorial Medal in 1994 and the [[Bunsen Medal]] in 2013. He is "External Scientific Member" of the [[Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry]] in Göttingen, member of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities|Göttingen Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Members: Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen (AdW) |url=https://adw-goe.de/it/members/personendetails/person/hermann-schmalzried/ |access-date=2022-08-20 |website=adw-goe.de}}</ref> the Leopoldina, corresponding member of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] and member of the [[Academia Europaea]] (1989).<ref name=AE /> He was awarded an honorary doctor at the University of Stuttgart in 2003.<ref name=Stuttgart />
